## Final work

Please email me your GitHub repos with your work by 12/10. Your project evaluation (24 points) will be based on this and feedback from your project mentor.
See the [Project Evaluation](../syllabus.qmd#project-evaluation) in the Syllabus for the criteria you will be evaluated on.

## Final presentation (IST 400 and 600)

**Date: 12/3**

**Points:** 12

Presentations will be 10 minutes + 3 minutes for questions. Your presentation should:

- Provide an overview of the project and what the goals were.

- Explain any obstacles you encountered.

- Explain what you accomplished.

- Demonstrate use of some of the concepts we touched on in class, such as proper use of GitHub.

### Examples

Students gave similar presentations about their OSPO internships in Spring 2026. You can find videos of their presentations along with their slides here:
[https://opensource.syracuse.edu/events/25-26-internship-presentations/](https://opensource.syracuse.edu/events/25-26-internship-presentations/).

### Tips

- 10 minutes goes by fast! Aim to have no more than 6 or 7 slides. Any more than that and you'll find yourself rushing to get through them.

- Practice your talk ahead of time! Even just one walk-through can make your presentations go much smoother, and give you an idea of how long your talk will actually take.

- Send your slides to your mentor ahead of time so they can give you feedback.


## Final papers (IST 600 only)

**Due: 12/10**

**Points:** 12

Papers should be short, JOSS-like articles that describe your project. Requirements:

- Length: the paper should be between 700 and 1800 words.

- It must have the following sections:

  * **Summary**: a description of the work for a non-specialist audience.

  * **Statement of need**: what problem does the software solve?

  * **State of the field**: compare to any existing software. If your project involved adding features to an existing software project, you can limit this to a statement about what the state of the software was before the start of your project.

  * **Software design**: explain what you did and your software architecture. Also mention any challenges you had, and how you addressed them.

    * Tip: This is a good place for a figure. Making a diagram can make it much easier to explain the software layout than trying to explain it in words. Make sure to include a caption for your figure and reference it in your main text.

  * **Research impact statement**: what is the impact of your work on the software package and/or the broader field. If this is a new package that hasn't been released yet, you can state what the potential impact is.

  * **AI usage disclosure**: describe if and how genAI was used in the software creation, documentation, or paper authoring.

  * **References**: Make sure to cite any references you use.

You can find an example JOSS paper [here](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.10806).

### Formats

I will accept Word, pdf, LaTeX, or markdown. If LaTeX or markdown, be sure to separately send the figures, so that it can be compiled. You will lose points if I cannot compile the LaTeX into a pdf or the markdown has syntax errors, so make sure you test this yourself (you may just want to send the pdf instead).

### Turning it in

Please email me your final report along with a link to the project GitHub or any other project materials by the end of the day on 12/10.
